items.title: AgensGraph 2.18 Released: Graph Database on PostgreSQL 18 with Expanded ISO GQL Support
items.summary: The AgensGraph Development Team is pleased to announce the release of AgensGraph v2.18.6.1, the latest version in the 2.18 series. AgensGraph is an open-source graph database, built on PostgreSQL 18.6, that runs SQL and graph queries over the same data, in the same transaction and even in the same statement.AgensGraph 2.18 is a major step toward the ISO GQL standard (ISO/IEC 39075), the international standard query language for property graphs. We are committed to bringing AgensGraph in line with GQL: 2.18 adds the first set of GQL clauses alongside openCypher, and more will follow in upcoming releases.Performance was the other focus of this release. Variable-length traversals now use the edge label's index at each hop, whereas 2.17 scanned the entire label at every hop. On the public soc-Pokec graph (30 million edges), a two-hop traversal that did not finish within 20 seconds in our tests on 2.17 now completes in milliseconds.HighlightsGQL clauses: LET, FOR, FILTER, NEXT, FINISH and INSERT, plus standalone ORDER BY, OFFSET and LIMIT clauses.Graph subqueries: CALL { }, OPTIONAL CALL, EXISTS { }, COUNT { }, COLLECT { } and VALUE { }, plus CALL ... YIELD to invoke PostgreSQL functions from Cypher.Based on PostgreSQL 18.6: asynchronous I/O, uuidv7(), virtual generated columns, OAuth authentication, B-tree skip scan and all PostgreSQL fixes through 18.6.Faster graph queries: variable-length traversals, pattern matching, label scans, EXISTS subqueries, path functions, sorting, grouping and counting of vertices and edges, ordering by vector distance, and the SET and DELETE clauses.Typed property columns: frequently queried properties can be stored as native typed columns and indexed like any other PostgreSQL column for faster filtering and sorting.Security: Cypher writes now enforce row-level security policies, and fixed-length patterns also enforce row-level security and privileges on labels they match without naming them.AI and Pythonagensgraph-python 2.1: a major new version of the Python driver, rebuilt on psycopg 3. It supports both synchronous and asynchronous code, runs Cypher and SQL in the same transaction, and returns vertices, edges and paths as native Python objects. Query results load straight into pandas, Polars or Arrow for analytics, and connection pooling, bulk loading and OpenTelemetry tracing are available.agensgraph-ai: integrations for building GraphRAG and knowledge-graph applications with LangChain (including a LangGraph checkpointer and store), LlamaIndex, LightRAG and cognee, plus Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that let AI assistants work with your graph.Graph and vectors together: with the pgvector extension (installed separately), graph data and vector embeddings live in the same database, so a single query can combine graph traversal with vector similarity search.UpgradingA 2.17 data directory cannot be used directly with 2.18. Upgrade with pg_upgrade, or dump with the 2.18 version of pg_dump and restore. Before you start, review what changed from 2.17. Installations already on 2.18.6.0 only need to replace the binaries and restart.LinksRelease notesDownloadsSourceDocker imagesDocumentationAbout AgensGraphAgensGraph is a multi-model graph database that extends PostgreSQL with openCypher and ISO GQL clauses, released under the Apache License 2.0. It has been developed since 2016 by SKAI Worldwide (formerly Bitnine).

items.title: Brume: FK-safe pseudonymization for PostgreSQL test and debug copies
items.summary: Brume 2.1, an open source (Apache 2.0) tool that creates deterministic, foreign-key-safe pseudonymized copies of PostgreSQL databases for testing, debugging and demos, is now available.Why Brume?Development teams often need realistic data to reproduce bugs, run tests or prepare demos, but copying production exposes real personal data. Classic masking scripts also tend to break referential integrity, which forces you to disable triggers, suspend constraints or repair broken joins by hand.Brume copies a targeted subset of a source database to a target database or to a .sql file, and transforms personal data on the fly, before anything is written. Foreign keys stay valid end-to-end on the target. Brume only reads from the source database.Key featuresColumn-level strategies: FAKE for realistic synthetic values, MASK for partial reveals, HASH for one-way hashing, NULLIFY to drop sensitive data, FPE_ID / FPE_UUID for format-preserving encryption of identifiers, and DATE_SHIFT to move dates while keeping their distribution.Deterministic output: transformations are keyed by your own secrets. The same input with the same secret always gives the same output, across all releases of a major version, so test fixtures and debug sessions stay stable from one run to the next.Referential integrity: format-preserving encryption rewrites primary keys and the foreign keys pointing to them consistently. With linked_columns, a value shared between tables that have no formal foreign key (for example, an email in both users and audit_logs) gets the same pseudonym everywhere.Subsetting: define row-level filters on any table (created_at >= '2025-01-01', tenant_id = 42...). Brume follows foreign keys up to a configurable depth, towards parents and children, to produce a small, self-contained and coherent extract.Declarative configuration: a single brume.yml file describes the strategy for each table and column, with semantic types (EMAIL, PHONE, IBAN, ADDRESS...) and JSONB paths to target nested fields. The file can be version-controlled and reviewed like code before any run.GDPRPseudonymization is one of the measures cited by GDPR Articles 25 and 32. Brume gives DPOs and security teams a reviewable, auditable description of how personal data is transformed before it leaves production.Compatibility and installationBrume supports PostgreSQL 12 to 18. Packages are available for Debian/Ubuntu (apt), RHEL/Fedora (dnf) and macOS (Homebrew).LinksWebsite and documentationQuickstartSource codeReleases

items.title: HeapDeck: an on-call monitor for PostgreSQL on iPhone and iPad
items.summary: HeapDeck is a new native app for engineers on call for PostgreSQL 13 to 19, on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.It opens on one health verdict with ten tiles. The Locks screen draws the tree from pg_blocking_pids() with the root blocker on top and counts the sessions that stopping it would free. Other screens cover pg_stat_activity, transaction ID wraparound and dead tuples, replication lag and slots, and pg_stat_statements.The app uses a direct connection or an SSH tunnel, with TLS and pinned fingerprints. No vendor server sits between the phone and the database. It works while open and sends no alerts, so it goes next to your existing alerting.Monitoring one server is free. HeapDeck Pro is a one-time in-app purchase that adds more servers and the actions: cancel, terminate, VACUUM, dropping a slot and writes.https://heapdeck.appPostgres, PostgreSQL and the Slonik Logo are trademarks or registered trademarks of the PostgreSQL Community Association of Canada, and used with their permission.HeapDeck is an independent client and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by the PostgreSQL Community Association of Canada, PostgreSQL Global Development Group, PostgreSQL Project, PostgreSQL Core Team, or PostgreSQL Community.

items.title: PG Observability Map 1.0.0 Released
items.summary: We are pleased to announce the initial release (1.0.0) of PG Observability Map, a interactive web-based tool designed to visualize and explore PostgreSQL observability, metrics, and internal diagnostic views.Key Features & Highlights:Interactive visual mapping of PostgreSQL system views, functions, and statistics.Architectural contextualization: each item is mapped directly to its corresponding PostgreSQL architectural section.Easy navigation across PostgreSQL versions (including PG 19 support).Lightweight interface, accessible directly via web browser.Links & Resources:Live Interactive Demo: meob.github.io/pg-observability-map/Source Code & Documentation: github.com/meob/pg-observability-map
